screens.title: AI awareness - Generative AI for Marketing Professionals

runs.t: Grasp the fundamentals of Generative AI and its applications in marketing. Understand the business and legal considerations, pros and cons of using Generative AI in marketing.
Develop skills in crafting effective AI prompts for marketing planning, content creation, graphic design, video, SEO / AEO, and more.
Learn about the leading Generative AI tools and learn how to integrate them in your marketing work for creativity, planning, and execution.
Prepare yourself for lifelong learning alongside AI:
Get ready to familiarize yourself with additional AI tools that pop up every day and create a personal/professional strategy for lifelong learning to stay ahead of machines as human marketing talent.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, especially computer systems.
The Stanford Cart, a small robot controlled by AI, becomes the first to navigate itself successfully.
The first intelligent industrial robot, the Famulus, is built in Germany.
The first AI program, called ELIZA, is created by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT. It simulates a conversation with a psychotherapist, though it has no real understanding of the conversation.
The term "artificial intelligence" is coined by John McCarthy at the Dartmouth Conference, which is considered the birth of AI as a field of study.
Alan Turing publishes his famous paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence," which introduces the idea of the "Turing Test" as a way to evaluate machine intelligence.
OpenAI's GPT-3 language model (ChatGPT) is released to the public, demonstrating remarkable abilities in natural language processing.
The world enters an AI revolution that continues since.

A type of artificial intelligence system that is loosely modeled after the human brain. Just like the brain is made up of interconnected neurons, a neural network is made up of interconnected nodes or units. Each node is a tiny computational machine that receives some input, does a simple operation on that input, and then passes the result on to other connected nodes. The weights of nodes is based on training/experience.

screens.title: What is the role of Marketing in organizations?

runs.t: What is the role of Marketing in organizations?
: Understanding customer personae, needs, preferences, and behaviors; analyze market trends and competitors; identify growth opportunities.
Developing marketing strategies aligned with organizational goals and objectives.
: Building and managing the organization's brand identity, positioning, and messaging. (Employer Branding)
Creating and executing campaigns utilizing various channels such as advertising, digital marketing, and public relations to reach and engage prospects, customers, investors, and employees.
Attracting new customers through targeted marketing initiatives, e.g. content marketing, social media marketing, and search engine optimization (SEO).
Providing sales with marketing collateral and resources to engage prospects. Create and maintain websites, presentations, brochures, etc.
Monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of marketing campaigns and initiatives. Optimize marketing efforts for continuous improvement.
